en.blurb_leader: %{name} is the chief rabbit of %{warren}Warren. The guardianship of all Warren rabbits has been entrusted to them by Inle. The chief rabbit is the highest authority in the Warren. The chief rabbit holds Warren meetings, determines mentors for new rusasirahs, and names new rabbits. To help them protect the Warren, Inle has given them nine lives. They typically take the suffix "star".
en.blurb_deputy: %{name} is %{warren}Warren's captain. The captain is the second in command, just below the chief rabbit. They advise the chief rabbit and organize daily patrols, alongside normal rabbit duties. Typically, a captain is personally appointed by the current chief rabbit. As dictated by the Rabbit Code, all captains must train at least one rusasirah before appointment. The captain succeeds the chief rabbit if they die or retire.
en.blurb_warrior: %{name} is a rabbit. Rabbits are adult rabbits who feed and protect their Warren. They are trained to hunt and fight in addition to the ways of the Rabbit Code. Rabbits are essential to the survival of a Warren, and usually make up the bulk of its members.
en.blurb_elder: %{name} is an elder. They have spent many moons serving their Warren, and have earned many moons of rest. Elders are essential to passing down the oral tradition of the Warren. Sometimes, rabbits may retire due to disability or injury. Whatever the circumstance of their retirement, elders are held in high esteem in the Warren and always eat before rabbits and healer rabbits.
en.blurb_medicine_cat: %{name} is a healer. Healer rabbits are the healers of the Warren. They treat injuries and illnesses with herbal remedies. Unlike rabbits, healer rabbits are not expected to hunt and fight for the Warren. In addition to their healing duties, healer rabbits also have a special connection to Inle. Every half-moon, they travel to their Warren's holy place to commune with Inle.
en.blurb_mediator: %{name} is a owsla. Owslas are not typically required to hunt or fight for the Warren. Rather, owslas are charged with handling disagreements between Warrenmates and disputes between Warrens. Some owslas train as rusasirahs to serve their Warren, while others may choose to become owslas later in life.
en.blurb_apprentice: %{name} is an rusasirah, in training to become a rabbit. Kits can be made rabbit rusasirahs at six moons of age, where they will learn how to hunt and fight for their Warren. Typically, the training of an rusasirah is entrusted to a single rabbit - their mentor. To build character, rusasirahs are often assigned the unpleasant and grunt tasks of Warren life. Rusasirahs usually take the suffix "-paw", to represent the path their paws take towards adulthood.
en.blurb_medcat_app: %{name} is a healer rusasirah, training to become a full healer. Kits can be made healer rusasirahs at six moons of age, where they will learn how to heal their Warrenmates and commune with Inle. Healer rusasirahs are typically chosen for their interest in healing and/or their connecting to Inle. Rusasirahs usually take the suffix "-paw", to represent the path their paws take towards adulthood.
en.blurb_mediator_app: %{name} is a owsla rusasirah, training to become a full owsla. Owslas are in charge of handling disagreements both within the Warren and between Warrens. Owsla rusasirahs are often chosen for their quick thinking and steady personality. Rusasirahs usually take the suffix "-paw", to represent the path their paws take towards adulthood.
en.blurb_kitten: %{name} is a kit. All rabbits below the age of six moons are considered kits. Kits are prohibited from leaving burrow in order to protect them from the dangers of the wild. Although they don't have any official duties in the Warren, they are expected to learn the legends and traditions of their Warren. They are protected by every rabbit in the Warren and always eat first. Kits usually take the suffix "-kit".
en.blurb_newborn: %{name} is a newborn kit. All rabbits below the age of six moons are considered kits. Kits are prohibited from leaving burrow in order to protect them from the dangers of the wild. Although they don't have any official duties in the Warren, they are expected to learn the legends and traditions of their Warren. They are protected by every rabbit in the Warren and always eat first. Kits usually take the suffix "-kit".
en.blurb_unknown: %{name} has an unknown rank. I guess they want to make their own way in life!
